name: DC Roofing LLC
subject: 🏠 Shawn, your certifications are trapped inside a picture on your site
body:
Hi Shawn,

I went through your website this week, all of it, which did not take long, because the whole thing is just one page.

That one page is hiding your best material. You are fully insured, certified in Mule-Hide, Dec Tech and CertainTeed, and you offer free estimates, but none of that is written anywhere a person or a search engine can read. It all sits inside the flyer picture at the very bottom of the page, and Google cannot read words inside a picture. Anyone who does not scroll to the very end never sees it. Even the flyer and your story disagree with each other: the flyer says 33 years of experience and 8 years in business, your About text says 34 and 9.

Meanwhile your actual work, the flat roof tie-ins, the coatings, the customized jobs, sits in galleries far down the page, past an About section that doubles back on itself with its Show More and Show Less copies.

The business behind that page is the gold standard, like your tagline says. The page itself is not. So I built you a proper one, and I have attached it to this email as three PDF files:

1. A new homepage: your own content and your own story, rebuilt, with an animated feel, your experience in clear numbers up top, your services laid out properly, a showcase of your real projects, and the trust points, insured, certified, free estimates, written as real text where homeowners and Google can actually find them.

2. A request a quote page: a dedicated form that asks for the type of roofing service first, tear off, re-cover, flat roof repair, storm damage and the rest, so every request that reaches you already tells you what the job is before you call back.

3. Updated brand guidelines for D.C. Roofing, built around your gold standard look, so your colors, fonts and star stay consistent everywhere your name appears.

Roofing websites are a big part of my work. Leal Roofing (leal-roofing.com) is a roofing site I built around clear services and easy quote requests. Severe Weather Roofing (severeweatherroofing.com) is another one of mine, built for storm damage work, where people need help fast and the site has to make calling effortless.

If you like the direction, I can put this on dcroofingllc.com and build out the rest of the pages with you. If not, the files are yours to keep as ideas, no hard feelings. A short reply is all it takes.

Best,
Hassan

attachments.name: D.C. Roofing - Request a Quote Page.pdf
